Chapter 2
Quality Planning
As with any SAP area, the success (and failure) of an SAP S/4HANA imple-
mentation project depends heavily on complete, correct, and compre-
hensive master data maintenance. Quality planning ensures that the
relevant master data is in place to enable you to perform quality inspec-
tion.
The quality planning area uses a particularly large amount of cross-functionality master
data from materials management (MM), production planning (PP), SAP S/4HANA Sales,
and other logistics areas. The quality planning process entails setting up not just the mas-
ter data in quality management (QM) but also the master data of other SAP S/4HANA
areas that integrate with QM. In this chapter, while we cover QM master data in detail,
we also provide a brief overview of master data of other areas for comprehension and
understanding only. Before accessing this data, it’s highly recommended that you dis-
cuss how you’ll use the data of these areas with the persons responsible for them. These
discussions usually result in new ideas for system use and highlight other potential
synergies in the area of QM integration. It’s also important to understand how the
sequence of master data maintenance generally helps in maintaining consistency in
predecessor-successor relationships. In this chapter, we follow the same sequence of
important QM master data creation.
Note
Throughout this book, we’ll either be covering the relevant master data or specific
master data settings that you’ll need to run the relevant business processes. At the
same time, we’ll be referring to the content of this chapter so that you ensure the QM
master data checklist is in place to run the relevant business processes.
Table 2.1 provides an initial overview of the relevant master data. We’ll explain the
most important points for QM in detail in this chapter. Because QM heavily integrates
with other SAP S/4HANA areas such as MM, embedded extended warehouse manage-
ment (EWM), plant maintenance (PM), or PP, it’s highly recommended to closely work
with consultants and business users of these areas to ensure complete and correct
availability of master data. Where possible or required, specific master data of another
SAP S/4HANA area that has direct implications on QM is discussed in this chapter—and
even throughout the book.

2.1 Quality Management View in Material Master
Let’s now delve into discussing and maintaining the important master data of Table 2.1.
2.1 Quality Management View in Material Master
When a company decides to implement QM to integrate its business processes with
logistics and the supply chain and to bring about improvements to business processes,
one of the very first master data maintenance tasks required is maintaining the Quality
management view of the material master.
The material master record in the SAP system is a complex and central entity, the pur-
pose of which is to control business and logistical processes. For the sake of clarity and
visibility, the system divides the material master record into different views. Maintain-
ing master data is a combined and collective responsibility of various departments or
persons. There is also the Quality management view (see Figure 2.1) of the material
master. If this view of the material isn’t available initially, the person responsible for
the material master record can add it later at any time. This has no effect on any part of
the logistics process (e.g., inventory management, procurement, production). The
functions for inspection-lot creation, stock posting, and—in particular—QM procure-
ment control are activated later, when the Quality management view is maintained
further.
You set up an inspection type in the Quality management view of the material master,
which acts as a control function for all subsequent activities. An inspection type is the
basic identifier for the different types of inspections available in the SAP system.
To add an inspection type to a material master, use Transaction MM02 or follow menu
path SAP  Logistics  Materials Management  Material Master  Material  Change 
Immediately. In the screen that appears, enter Material “RM17” and Plant “1710”, and
then click Quality Management to go to the Quality management view, as shown in
Figure 2.1.

Tips and Tricks
If the Quality management view hasn’t been previously maintained, use Transaction
MM01 to create the Quality management view of the material master first.
Figure 2.1 shows the Quality management view of material RM17 for plant 1710, which
includes the following important fields:
 QM Material Auth. (authorization) helps to control who is authorized to perform
inspection-related tasks on this material. This field also controls the digital signature
in SAP, which is discussed in Chapter 3.
 GR Processing Time is the average number of working days it takes it to process an
inspection lot. The system uses this information during material requirements
planning (MRP) to take the inspection duration into account while planning pro-
curement, production, or availability of a material.
 A Catalog Profile consists of defects and defect locations and is available during
quality notification creation (see Chapter 12 for more details).
 Material Status is the control function that allows or disallows the functions or busi-
ness processes possible for this material. For example, a control function such as a
material may be blocked from procurement, or the material may be obsolete.
 Inspection Interval denotes the frequency with which a batch-managed material under-
goes recurring (repeat) inspection. Recurring inspection is discussed in Chapter 9.
© 

61
2.1 Quality Management View in Material Master
The control functions in the Procurement Data area are covered in Chapter 4.
Click on the Insp. Setup button in Figure 2.1 to go to Figure 2.2, which shows the initial
screen of Inspection Setup Data. Because no inspection type existed when you first
clicked on the Insp. Setup button, you’ll find a blank screen.
You can incorporate or set up a new inspection type with the Inspection Types button
shown in Figure 2.2. Inspection type 01 is relevant for the quality inspection of raw
material (or other procured materials) on goods receipt against a purchase order. It’s
important to note that assignment of an inspection type to a material is plant-specific.
You can assign more than one inspection type to a material. For example, a batch-man-
aged finished good with a shelf-life expiration date is inspected on its production com-
pletion (known as goods receipt inspection against production order), but then the
same finished good also undergoes periodic inspection if it remains unsold and its
batch’s shelf life is about to expire (known as recurring inspection).
Figure 2.2 Inspection Setup Data

2 Quality Planning
62
Consider another example: the company’s business process requires inspection of a raw
material at the supplier’s premises for compliance with important quality parameters
prior to its delivery into the company’s warehouse (known as source inspection). The
same raw material will again go through another round of quality inspection when the
goods reach the company’s warehouse (known as goods receipt inspection against the
purchase order). This requires activation of two different inspection types. The first
inspection type is for inspection at the supplier premises, and the second inspection
type is for inspection at the company’s premises. When you want to activate a specific
inspection type, you need to ensure that the Active checkbox is selected. Due to changes
in the business process, if a particular inspection type is no longer needed, simply dese-
lecting the Active checkbox deactivates it. This is the easiest way to deactivate an inspec-
tion type at any time. You can also delete the entire inspection type, if needed.
Based on your business needs and at any point in time, you can add a new inspection
type or make changes to control indicators of an already existing inspection type in
Inspection Setup.
Warning
On deactivating or deleting an inspection type, you first have to ensure that there is no
quality stock.
Now, click Insp. type det. (inspection type details; the right button [the magnifying
glass]) to view the details of the fields and other options available for inspection type
01. Table 2.2 explains some of the important fields of Figure 2.2.
Control Indicator Effects
Post to Insp. Stock Posts a goods movement to the inspection stock for the
material. Only in the QM area, within the scope of the
usage decision, can you release anything out of quality
inspection stock. In an exceptional case, the movement
type itself enables the system to determine whether to
post the quantity to inspection stock.
Insp. with Mat Spec. With this indicator set, you can use a material specifica-
tion to carry out an inspection. An inspection that uses a
material specification can be in addition to, or even
replace, an inspection that uses a routing or a master rec-
ipe. You need to completely maintain a material specifica-
tion for the material to carry out an inspection. Refer to
Section 2.12 on how to set up a material specification.
Table 2.2 Inspection Types Setup
© 

63
2.1 Quality Management View in Material Master
Insp. with Task List With this indicator set, the system requires a task list for
an inspection with the inspection lot. The decision on
whether a routing or a master recipe is required is made
during inspection data maintenance in the material mas-
ter record. The system can only determine the sample size
after assignment of the task list to the inspection lot. In
Chapter 3, you’ll see that when the system is unable to
find and assign a task list to an inspection lot, it’s unable
to calculate the sample size.
Insp. by Configuration If this indicator is set, the system takes configurations
from the sales order or production order into account in
inspection-lot creation.
Automatic Assignment The system tries to automatically assign a routing, an
inspection plan, or a material specification to the inspec-
tion lot.
Inspect Charcs If you want characteristic-based results recording, you
have to use a routing, an inspection plan, or a material
specification for the inspection. Characteristic-based
results recording is a prerequisite for characteristic-based
dynamic modification. You can select a dynamic modifi-
cation level in an inspection plan.
Smpl. Procedure A procedure to determine the size of the sample in an
inspection. The sampling procedure also defines the valu-
ation type used for results recording (attributive, variable,
manual, etc.).
This field is of significance only in an inspection that
doesn’t use a routing, master recipe, or material specifica-
tion. If you enter a sampling procedure here, the system
calculates the total sample size from the lot size. Select a
sampling procedure that uses a valuation mode without
valuation parameters.
In the case of an inspection without a routing, master rec-
ipe, or material specification, you have the following
options to determine the inspection scope for a specific
material:
 100% inspection
 Specify a percentage
 Specify a sampling procedure without valuation
parameters
Control Indicator Effects
Table 2.2 Inspection Types Setup (Cont.)

2 Quality Planning
64
100% Inspection There are two possible business scenarios that you need
to consider while setting up this indicator:
 Inspect without routing, master recipe, or material
specification
The system creates the sample size as equal to the cre-
ated lot.
 Inspect with routing, master recipe, or material speci-
fication
The sample size of the created lot is the same as the
lot size. The sampling procedure set down in the
inspection plan or specification isn’t taken into
account in the sample determination process for the
inspection characteristics. Instead, the system uses
sample determination rules, which are preset in the
configuration. The sample size of the created charac-
teristics depends on whether the base unit of measure
has decimal places. If the base unit of measure does
have decimal places, the sample size of the character-
istic is always 1; if the base unit of measure doesn’t
have decimal places, 100% of the lot size should be
inspected in sample units of measure (rounded up) for
the characteristic.
Here, the dependencies are that if in addition to either
100% inspection, Inspect with Task List, or Insp. by Config-
uration indicators, you also set the Skips Allowed charac-
teristic, nothing changes in the sample calculation.
However, the system does check whether the characteris-
tic is to be inspected or not.
Inspection % This field is of significance only in an inspection that
doesn’t use a routing, master recipe, task list, or material
specification. In this case, the system calculates the over-
all sample size using this percentage value from the
inspection lot size.
Manual Sample Calc. Set this indicator if you want to manually trigger the sam-
ple calculation for the inspection lot.
Manual Sample Entry If this checkbox is selected, then you need to manually
enter the sample size for the inspection of this inspection
lot. This characteristic is only taken into account in
inspections that don’t use a routing, task list, or material
specification.
Control Indicator Effects
Table 2.2 Inspection Types Setup (Cont.)
© 

65
2.1 Quality Management View in Material Master
Dyn. Mod. Rule This is for the dynamic modification rule. It contains defi-
nitions of the inspection levels and the conditions that
cause inspection levels to change. This field is significant
only in an inspection that doesn’t use a routing or mate-
rial specification. If you enter a dynamic modification rule
here, a quality level for the material, plant, and inspection
type is set, and when the quality level is created automat-
ically, the system calculates the dynamic modification cri-
teria for the inspection-lot origin. If, in addition to the
sample size, you control using a sampling procedure, the
system checks whether the combination of dynamic
modification rule and sampling procedure is permitted
(permitted relationships). Refer to Chapter 3, which cov-
ers the dynamic modification rule in detail.
Skips Allowed If you set this indicator, then the system allows skipping
results recording for inspection characteristics when it
calculates the sample size of the lot.
The characteristic takes effect in the inspection lot if it’s
set in the QM inspection data of the material for the
inspection type in question. If the characteristic isn’t set
in the dynamic modification process, the system selects
the next nonskip inspection level instead of a skip level. If
all the characteristics to be inspected in an inspection lot
have the Skip status, it results in a skip inspection lot.
In the case of a skip lot, if both skips and automatic usage
decision are allowed, inspection-lot processing is carried
out without any user intervention. A time delay can be set
for this in the configuration. This triggers unrestricted
stock at the goods receipt stage because the lot quantity
is immediately posted to unrestricted-use stock.
In the QM control function in procurement (quality infor-
mation record), you can make a setting that skips the
goods receipt inspections. You can also specify for the
material in the inspection data that an inspection is to be
carried out only for the first goods receipt per order or
production order. To prevent individual characteristics
from being skipped, proceed as follows:
 Assign characteristic weightings to the characteristics
to prevent skips.
 Assign sampling procedures to the characteristics that
don’t permit stage changes.
Control Indicator Effects
Table 2.2 Inspection Types Setup (Cont.)

2 Quality Planning
66
Automatic UD If you set this indicator, the system can automatically
make usage decisions for inspection lots. The inspection
lots have to fulfill the following conditions:
 All characteristics are completed.
 No characteristic has been rejected.
 No defects have been recorded, and no quality notifi-
cation has been created.
The lead time set in configuration must have expired.
Inspection lots with the status Skip Lot can also be con-
sidered here.
If an automatic usage decision can’t be made, you’ll have
to make it manually. The system records an automatic
usage decision in the long text that accompanies the
usage decision.
Chapter 3 shows you how to make automatic usage deci-
sions for skipped inspection lots.
Avg. Insp. Duration Specifies the average duration, in days, of the inspection
for every inspection type. If the start date of the inspec-
tion is entered during inspection-lot creation, the system
calculates the end date using the average inspection time
entered in this field. Conversely, if the end date of the
inspection is entered during inspection-lot creation, the
system calculates the start date using the average inspec-
tion time entered in this field.
Q-Score Procedure The coded ID of the procedure that the system uses to cal-
culate the quality score. You can maintain one quality
score procedure per inspection type in the material mas-
ter record. The system transfers the information main-
tained in this field to the inspection lot record on
inspection lot creation.
In the simplest procedure, the quality score is taken from
the code for the usage decision. In another procedure, the
quality score is calculated on the basis of the scrap share
in the inspected characteristics.
Allowed Scrap Share Some quality score procedures require an allowed scrap
share to calculate the quality score. In normal cases, the
scrap share is set to be half the acceptable quality level
(AQL) value.
Control Indicator Effects
Table 2.2 Inspection Types Setup (Cont.)
© 

67
2.1 Quality Management View in Material Master
Control Lot Creation This control applies to goods receipt for inspection lot ori-
gins 01, 04, 05, and 08.
You can make the following settings:
 <Space>: One inspection lot per goods receipt docu-
ment item. In other words, one inspection lot is cre-
ated for each goods receipt document item.
 X: One inspection lot per purchase order item or order
item and batch. If you set this value, the system cre-
ates an inspection lot only for the first goods receipt
for each purchase order item or production order, or, if
the material is managed in batches, only for the first
goods receipt per purchase order item or production
order and batch. This setting is restricted to the inspec-
tion lot origins For Purchase Order (Inspection Lot Ori-
gin 01) and For Production Order (Inspection Lot Origin
04).
 1: One inspection lot per material document, material,
and batch. If you set this value, the system opens only
one inspection lot per material and batch (in the case
of batch management) for a material document (i.e.,
within a goods receipt transaction). This can occur if
several purchase orders or several partial deliveries of
the same material are processed within one goods
receipt transaction.
 2: One inspection lot per material and batch. If you set
this value, the system opens only one inspection lot
per material and batch (in the case of batch manage-
ment). This setting is useful only for materials that
require batch management.
In the case of X, 1, and 2, if the stock of the inspection lot
that was created with the first goods receipt isn’t com-
pletely discharged or its usage decision made when fur-
ther partial deliveries are received, these goods receipt
quantities are added to this stock. In the case of 1 and 2, if
Skip Lot is set, there is no direct change of the stock type
from In Quality Inspection to Unrestricted Use. Instead, a
transfer posting takes place as part of an automatic
usage decision with a time delay.
Control Indicator Effects
Table 2.2 Inspection Types Setup (Cont.)

2 Quality Planning
68
Tips and Tricks
When you’re maintaining the control indicator of the inspection data, we recommend
that you use the predefined and default configuration settings for each inspection
type. This is important because different entries for the same inspection type cause
different materials to be used or cause difficulties with the inspection-lot generation
process.
If a special inspection lot control process is required on the material level for the same
inspection type, this must be carefully documented in each individual case.
For more information, see Chapter 3, which covers the configuration details of main-
taining default values for inspection types.
Table 2.3 contains a selective list of inspection types of respective inspection origins
that we cover in various chapters of this book. The last column is the number of the
chapter in which you’ll find detailed configuration, master data setup, requirements, or
business processes that use the specific inspection type.
Individual QM order This characteristic specifies that you need to create an
individual QM order with an account assignment when
the system creates an inspection lot for this inspection
type. If you set this characteristic, you’re specifying that
an individual QM order should be opened for this combi-
nation of material and inspection type.
If the field for the QM order is filled and the characteristic
for individual QM orders is set, this field is taken into
account only if the system is unable to create an individ-
ual QM order due to a missing account assignment in the
inspection lot. A prerequisite for creating an individual
QM order is that the inspection lot contains an allocation
provision such as sales order, cost center, or plant.
QM Order A number that uniquely identifies the QM order to which
the costs are to be charged. The QM order specified in the
material master record in the inspection data is used as a
template for inspection-lot creation if an individual QM
order hasn’t been created for the inspection lot.

Note
In project discussions, requests are often made to create new inspection types to meet
specific business needs, such as inspection types that reflect different strategies for
incoming inspections for fundamentally different materials. Even if you configure new
or extra inspection types, the problem still remains. This is because the inspection ori-
gins to which you have to assign the inspection type are preconfigured and delivered.
You therefore have no choice but to individually change the relevant control indicators
under Inspection Data in the Quality management view of the material. In such a case,
the only configuration tasks are to customize the short name of the inspection type
and the global control indicator for each existing inspection type. For this reason, we
don’t recommend that you create new inspection types to meet this business need.
Chapter 3 shows how you can configure a new inspection type and use it in business
processes.
2.2 Master Record
This section covers the important QM master record, as well as other logistics areas
needed in the SAP S/4HANA system to run business processes.
2.2.1 Change Master Record
To manage the different versions of a drawing that belongs to a material master record,
an inspection plan, or an inspection method, for example, it may be a good idea to also
assign a version to every material. You can link every version of the material master
record with a change master record. A change master record brings far greater control

2.2 Master Record
and visibility to changes made to the QM master record, such as an inspection method

Note
See Chapter 13, which contains an example of using a change number to manage
changes to an inspection plan.
2.2.2 Business Partner Master Record
The supplier master record contains all the necessary information about a supplier
from the purchasing and accounting points of view. In addition, the buyer can set a
lock under the Lock Data option for quality reasons. This lock contains the same list
entries as those in the quality info record for delivery control on the material supplier
level. The details of the contact persons for purchasing and QM are stored in the part-
ner data of the supplier master.
The customer master record, on the other hand, contains all the necessary information
about a customer from the point of view of sales and accounting. The buyer can also set
a lock, if necessary, for quality reasons. This master record also contains partner data,
such as the contact person in the customer’s company. It can be useful to maintain the
details of a contact person responsible for quality matters.
2.2.3 Batch Master
If the company maintains an externally procured material or an in-house material
through batch management, the system creates a batch master record using Transac-
tion MSC1N or menu path Logistics  Materials Management  Material Master  Batch 
Create. With the relevant configuration settings in place, the system can automatically
assign a batch number, or a user can do so manually for goods movements or for pro-
cess or production orders. If batch management is active for a material, the system
requires a batch number during inspections and can also assign the inspection lot data
to the batches.
An important consideration for process industries is that it’s a requirement to separate
various batches of a material according to their different properties. To this end,
batches are divided into different classes, which are defined in advance in the batch
characteristics. If during the inspection a batch fulfills the specification of a batch char-
acteristic, it’s assigned to the relevant batch class. If a material with the required prop-
erties is subsequently used for further processing or for a sales order, the batch
classification finds the appropriate material. You also need the batch master record for
order processing in production planning for process industries (PP-PI).

72

location 0001. The system automatically fills in the date of manufacture, shelf-life
expiration date/best-before date (SLED/BBD), and next inspection date while running

as well as the business processes that either fill up or automatically update the various

2.2.4 Production Resources and Tools
All the resources required for production, such as documents, operating supplies, test
equipment, tools, equipment, and so on, are within the scope of production resources/
tools (PRTs). You need to assign the PRTs to the operations and inspection characteris-
tics of a task list. Depending on the PRT type, the master record can be a material, doc-
ument, PRT master record, or equipment master record.
© 

73
2.5 Work Center
Note
See Chapter 7 on QM integration with PM (test equipment management), which also
covers various types of PRTs. The chapter includes cross-elements from quality plan-
ning, repairs and maintenance (calibration tests), and their master records (equipment).
2.3 Master Recipe or Routing
In this task list type, the work-scheduling function records all elements in the task plan-
ning area, and the QM function records all data for inspection planning. The produc-
tion steps and capacities are linked to the work centers, and the required control
functions for the production order are determined. The elements of inspection plan-
ning, inspection characteristics, sampling procedure, and so on are fully integrated
into the master recipe or routing.
2.4 Reference Operation Set
The reference operation set contains virtually all the objects and functions of the rout-
ing. It’s used mainly as a task list template for variations of a production procedure or as
a general template. The individual operations in the reference operation set are refer-
enced for this purpose in the routing or in the inspection plan (a fixed reference; every
change in the reference operation set affects the inspection plan and the routing).
Note
The reference operation set, routing, and inspection plan are the same in terms of their
structure and essential functions. This makes navigating in the different task list types
quite simple for the inspection planner, who has to maintain the quality-relevant data
in all task list types.
Chapter 5 on production processes also covers details of the master recipe, routing, and
reference operation set master data.
2.5 Work Center
A quality work center is the physical or virtual location in which a user performs related
quality inspection activities. A work center is always plant-specific. The work center is a
master record that’s important mainly for PP and controlling. It’s likewise usually
maintained by the Production Planning and Control department. Every work center is
assigned to a cost center so that the accounting department can analyze quality costs.
To this end, the system calculates the costs that arise from the work performed at the
work center on the basis of the allocation records for the individual cost centers.

2 Quality Planning
74
To create a work center for quality inspection, use Transaction CRQI or follow menu
path SAP  Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Basic Data  Work Center 
QM Work Center  Work Center  Create.
In the screen that appears, enter Plant “1710” and Work Center “QCLAB”, and then enter
the Work Center Category “0003”. There are various categories available in the SAP sys-
tem. A category groups together similar work being performed at the work center. Exam-
ples of work center categories are machine, labor, production line, and quality inspection.
On the screen shown in Figure 2.4, enter a short text to provide some details about the
type of work center and the work performed in it. A person responsible is the in-charge
or supervisor of the quality control lab. This can be an individual or a position. In gen-
eral, the position option is preferred because a person may move to another depart-
ment or leave the job.

and version, and the system automatically copies all the information from the refer-

2.10 Sampling Procedure
A sampling procedure enables the system to calculate the sample size of the inspection
lot for quality inspection and then inspect and record its results. In a sampling proce-
dure, you determine the sample size and the valuation rules for the inspection charac-
teristics.
© 

91
2.10 Sampling Procedure
Example
A supplier delivers 100 kg of PET chips (a raw material used in making plastic bottles)
against a purchase order. The system should be able to calculate a sample size of 5 kg
because the sampling procedure stipulates inspecting 5% of the delivered goods as the
sample size for inspection.
To create a sampling procedure, use Transaction QDV1 or follow menu path SAP  Logis-
tics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Inspection Planning  Basic Data  Sample 
Sampling Procedure  Create. On the initial screen that appears, enter sampling proce-
dure “FIX10” to denote the relevancy and the settings made. Press (Enter), and the screen
shown in Figure 2.15 appears.
From the Sampling Type dropdown, you can choose one of the four available sampling
types:
 100 Fixed sample
Regardless of the quantity delivered by the supplier or produced in house, the sys-
tem always calculates a fixed sample quantity for inspection. For example, for a pro-
duced/procured quantity of either 100 kg or 1,000 kg, the system calculates the
fixed sample size of 3, if the sample size is 3.
 200 100% Inspection
Regardless of the quantity delivered by the supplier or produced in house, the com-
plete quantity is available for inspection.
 300 Using sampling scheme
A sampling scheme uses an incremental method of calculating sample size. The big-
ger the produced/procured material is, the smaller the overall sample size available
for inspection can be. For example, for a procured quantity of up to 100 kg, the sam-
ple size is 5 kg, whereas for a procured quantity between 101 kg and 1,000 kg, the
sample size is 8 kg. It’s impractical to inspect a large sample quantity if the overall
delivered quantity is too big.
 400 Sample percentage
A percentage of the total produced/procured quantity is available as a sample size
for quality inspection. For example, for a procured or produced quantity of 200 kg of
material, the sample size is 4 kg because the sample percentage is defined as 2%.
Whenever the system creates an inspection lot for produced or procured material, it
automatically and immediately calculates the sample size. The purpose of a sampling
procedure is to be able to calculate the sample size for quality inspection from the total
inspection lot quantity.

 A manual decision is required for attributive characteristics (i.e., characteristics for

2.11 Inspection Plan
You use the inspection plan’s task list type in QM to process procurement-, production-,
or sales-related quality inspections. Its typical application areas are model inspections,
goods receipt inspections, goods issue inspections, and goods receipts from produc-
tion. Its main functions are the same as those of the routing. Besides assigning to the
material, you can also assign the following to the inspection plan:
 Material and business partner (supplier)
 Material and business partner (customer)
The inspection plan can include the reference operation set in their operations and
thus use a modular system of operations and inspection characteristics.
In the SAP S/4HANA system, the inspection plan is the production-based task list type
that’s available in PP and PP-PI. From a QM perspective, this has the advantage that the
inspection plan is structured in exactly the same way as the routing and thus already

2.11.3 Material Assignment
Material assignment functionality in the inspection plan enables you to significantly
reduce your master data maintenance efforts. This is achieved by assigning multiple
materials, suppliers, or customers with the same inspection requirements into one
task list group (inspection plan) as long as they have the same set of operations and
master inspection characteristics of the materials.
Example
Your company produces and packs a product (e.g., tomato ketchup) in different sizes.
For each product’s size, there’s a separate material master code available in the system.
Instead of creating one inspection plan for each size of the product, you can create one
inspection plan and assign multiple material codes to it via the material assignment
functionality.
Because inspection plans are also used for supplier-procured materials or finished
goods sold to customers, you can introduce further visibility and controls by using
inspection plans that are specific to suppliers or customers.

2.12 Material Specification
Material specification is managed without reference to any plant-specific master
inspection characteristics. This alternative to the general inspection plan (with opera-
tions and characteristics) in the SAP system provides a simple variant of the inspection
plan structuring process that doesn’t contain any operations. Simply put, a work regu-
lation for quality inspections is prepared in the material specification, using com-
pletely maintained master inspection characteristics or general characteristics. This
avoids redundant or duplicate data entry efforts or information in the SAP system.
To create a material specification, use Transaction QS61 or follow menu path SAP 
Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Inspection Planning  Material Spec-
ification  Edit.
On the initial screen that appears, enter Material “RM17”, and press (Enter) or choose
Characteristics, and the screen in Figure 2.30 appears. Here, just like with the QM
inspection plan, you can also use master inspection characteristics of other plants
while creating the material specification. When assigning a master inspection charac-
teristic in the material specification, the system looks for complete copy model or ref-
erence characteristic. If the master inspection characteristic is either of the two, it’s
possible to assign it while creating a material specification. However, a material speci-
fication doesn’t allow usage of an incomplete copy model of a master inspection char-
acteristic.
QMHT10 is a reference master inspection characteristic; therefore, all information,
such as decimal places or upper and lower specification limits, is automatically copied
from the master inspection characteristic when you create a material specification and
is initially available in noneditable mode. Notice the Lock icon in the Ref column that
shows the master inspection characteristic is a reference characteristic. You can unlock
this lock and make desired changes for the master inspection characteristic in the
material specification.
